data.one_liner: A key-value storage solution built on sqflite with encryption and time-to-live support.
data.what_it_does: It provides a browser localStorage-like interface in Flutter for storing Dart JSON maps. Data is backed by SQLite, can be fully encrypted using secure storage for keys, and supports item expiration via time-to-live (TTL).
use_when: You need simple key-value storage for JSON maps with optional encryption.
You want automatic expiration (TTL) for cached key-value data.
You need batch processing performance for writing multiple items.
avoid_when: you need reactive state management tied directly to storage changes.
your target Android minSdk is lower than 18.
strengths: Built-in data encryption using secure storage for keys.
Supports time-to-live (TTL) expiration on stored items.
weaknesses: Relies on a singleton architecture which may limit multi-instance configurations.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick if you need a standard lightweight key-value store without SQL overhead or built-in encryption needs.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick if you need raw relational SQL queries rather than a key-value interface.

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick if you want a type-safe reactive SQL database library with code generation.

data.minimal_example:
JsonStore jsonStore = JsonStore();
Map<String, dynamic> json = await jsonStore.getItem('counter');
